title: Streamline shard activation and introduce checksum ledger for weight manifests
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: We've accumulated multiple quick fixes around shard activation and tokenizer initialization that increase tail latency and complicate boot sequence observability. Different weight formats write inconsistent checksum metadata and the runtime performs full-materialization of shards before tokenizer handoff, which blocks warm starts and increases OOM risk on memory-constrained hosts.

Scope: Replace ad-hoc checksum fields with a small, append-only checksum ledger (per-manifest) that supports incremental verification and fast skip-on-read. Decouple tokenizer initialization from full shard materialization by introducing a 'prefetch-light' path that exposes vocab/merges/weights-needed-for-init only. Add backpressure-aware shard activator to avoid parallel materialization storms during heavy scale-ups. Upgrade protobuf dependency and the manifest schema to v2 to support the ledger, keeping a migration shim for older manifests.

Goals / Success criteria:
- Reduce median model cold-start time (tokenizer-ready) by >= 35% for common L1 model families measured on prod-sim benchmark.
- Reduce concurrent peak memory during boot by >= 20% on 16GB GPU nodes.
- No customer-facing API changes; manifests remain backward-compatible for hosts with old runtime for one rollout window.
- CI includes fuzz tests simulating partial-shard reads and corrupted-ledger scenarios.

Design highlights and trade-offs:
- Checksum ledger: small append-only log stored alongside manifest. Allows incremental verification; cost is slightly larger manifest write and migration complexity. We chose ledger vs embedding per-shard CRC fields because ledger enables atomic batch commits and efficient pruning.
- Prefetch-light: only load tokenizer assets + first pass of KV-block headers to allow tokenizer handshake and streaming generation to start. Trade-off: may require extra small read latency later when full materialization completes; mitigated by background activation and caching.
- Protobuf upgrade: bump to 4.x (internal ABI changes). We will implement a migration shim that can read both proto v1 and v2 manifests to avoid fleet-wide cascade. Short-term risk of subtle parsing differences; added integration tests mitigate.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration tests cover ledger creation, read, and incremental verify paths.
- Production-sim benchmark demonstrates target latency/memory improvements.
- Rollout plan (canary -> 25% -> 100%) in console runbook and auto-fallback on checksum mismatch.
- Code review and sign-off from Serving Runtime lead and Tokenizer owner.

Notes on rollout and monitoring:
- Console dashboards: new per-manifest metric checkpoint.verify_time_ms and shard.activation_backpressure_events.
- Automatic fallback: if ledger verification fails in canary, runtime falls back to previous full-verify path and emits incident alert.
- Data migration: manifests written after rollout will include ledger. Older manifests are supported by shim; domain cleanup job scheduled Cycle+2 to purge legacy footprints.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Kickoff: scoped with runtime, tokenizer, and infra. Diego to prototype ledger writer; Ava to draft migration doc. Action: spike to measure tokenizer-only init cost. (PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Shard+Activation+Ledger)

2026-02-24 - Spike results: tokenizer-only init reduces tokenizer-ready time by ~42% on L1-medium models. Memory sampling shows ~18% peak reduction - close to target. Decision: proceed with ledger + prefetch-light path.

2026-02-28 - Design review (ops + security): agreed to append-only ledger with signed checksum entries. Security asked for KMS-signed manifest header; we will add optional signature field. Issue: protobuf bump requires updating our hermetic build images. Action: infra tasked (ENG-130402) to provide updated builder by 2026-03-08.

2026-03-02 - Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2378 implemented ledger append/read and a basic prefetch-light path. Bench harness in repo under runtime/bench/manifest-boot. Asked reviewers to test with legacy manifests.

2026-03-04 - Code review feedback: Performance review from SRE (J. Patel) - suggestion to add backpressure token bucket per-host to limit concurrent materializations. Diego updated design to use a leaky-bucket with adjustable window. Also added additional logging for partial-verify failures.

2026-03-05 - QA plan: create fuzz suite for partial-shard reads and corrupted-ledger entries. QA to run across linux-16gb and linux-48gb builders. Next steps: finalize PR, merge migration shim, and coordinate canary rollout after infra builder update.
